title: A Ember for the Hollow
premise: Jude Vane has spent nine years as the royal food-taster, swallowing poison in measured doses and keeping the ledgers of the Hollow Guild, which trades in impossible things: borrowed years, bottled grief, names. When the border wards collapse on the night every star goes dark, Jude learns his own soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain before he was born—the price his mother paid to keep him alive through a plague winter. The court's tithe-collector has come to collect the rest of him, and with each day the stars stay dead, Jude loses another memory. To survive, he must descend into the Undercourt, out-bargain its patient king using the guild's own ledgers against it, and decide whether a self assembled from other people's payments is worth stealing back. He wins his soul at the cost of the guild itself, relights the stars with the debt everyone owed him, and chooses to remember everything—even what it cost.
about_author: Ivo Coldharbour is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate sales and claims to have found one ledger that could not be explained. They write fantasy about paperwork, hunger, and the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Taster's Portion
chapters.summary: Jude Vane's POV. A routine morning tasting for the Queen turns strange when a dish arrives that no kitchen admits making. Jude recognizes the flavor of memory-wine from the Hollow Guild's ledgers. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath practiced calm.

chapters.title: Ledgers of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Jude balances the guild's books by candlelight, cataloguing trades: a widow's laughter sold for her son's fever breaking. His own name appears in an old margin, redacted. Emotional beat: the comfort of order beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Small Poisons
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Jude's POV. How a starving boy became a taster, building immunity dish by dish under Master Corvel's cold instruction. Emotional beat: survival as a discipline, tenderness as a liability.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Jude wakes to total darkness over the capital; the border wards have fallen simultaneously. Panic in the streets, guards deserting. Emotional beat: vertigo—the invisible man suddenly visible in a city with no sky.

chapters.title: A Visitor With a Receipt
chapters.summary: The tithe-collector Sable arrives at Jude's door holding a contract signed in his mother's hand. She claims his soul is already half-owned by the court beneath the mountain. Emotional beat: cold recognition—he was never free.

chapters.title: What Mother Paid
chapters.summary: Jue searches his childhood memories of the plague winter, finding gaps shaped like transactions. He visits his mother's grave and finds it freshly turned. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Guild Assembles
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Ossen calls an emergency meeting; impossible things are failing across the city—borrowed years expiring early, bottled grief leaking. Jude's POV among traders who fear him knowing too much. Emotional beat: belonging that was always conditional.

chapters.title: Terms of Forfeiture
chapters.summary: Sable returns with a deadline: thirty days until the tithe completes and Jude becomes the Undercourt's property outright. Each passing starless day takes one of his memories. Emotional beat: terror made bureaucratic.

chapters.title: First Loss: The Sea
chapters.summary: Jude realizes he can no longer remember the ocean where he grew up. He writes down everything he still knows, filling notebooks. Emotional beat: mourning himself in advance.

chapters.title: The Road Beneath the Wards
chapters.summary: Jude leaves the capital with guild smuggler Brannic, descending toward the mountain through countryside where wards lie broken like fallen fences. Emotional beat: reluctant companionship, first hope.

chapters.title: Village of the Unremembered
chapters.summary: They find a village whose residents traded their memories to survive the plague—smiling, hollow, hospitable. Jude sees his possible future. Emotional beat: horror wearing a welcoming face.

chapters.title: Brannic's Price
chapters.summary: Brannic reveals he once sold his daughter's name to the Undercourt and has been searching for a way to buy it back for twenty years. Emotional beat: guilt transmuted into shared resolve.

chapters.title: The Tollgate of Teeth
chapters.summary: At the mountain's mouth, a gate demands payment in something irreplaceable. Jude pays with his immunity—every poison tolerance he built, surrendered. Emotional beat: sacrifice of the very thing that kept him alive.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: POV alternates between Jude above ground and fragments of his mother's ledger entries below, revealing she descended this same road pregnant and desperate. Emotional beat: following a ghost's footsteps.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Jude enters the Undercourt: a mirrored inversion of the royal palace, lit by the stolen stars embedded in its ceiling. Emotional beat: awful beauty, recognition of where the sky went.

chapters.title: Audience with the Patient King
chapters.summary: The King of the Undercourt, courteous and ancient, explains the terms: souls here are currency, and Jude's has been appreciating for twenty-six years. Emotional beat: being appraised like goods.

chapters.title: The Ledger Room
chapters.summary: Jude discovers the Undercourt keeps accounts too—and they mirror the Hollow Guild's books. Someone has been feeding it entries for generations. Emotional beat: the enemy speaks his professional language.

chapters.title: An Old Debt of the Crown
chapters.summary: Jude finds the original contract: the royal family itself has been selling subjects' souls to fund the wards for two centuries. His mother was one entry among thousands. Emotional beat: betrayal scaled to a kingdom.

chapters.title: Sable's Second Face
chapters.summary: Jude confronts Sable, learning she was once human—a taster before him, whose collection failed. She warns him the King always wins because debt is the court's native tongue. Emotional beat: pity for the thing hunting him.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Memory Auction
chapters.summary: To buy audience time, Jude auctions his own memories in the Undercourt's market, watching strangers bid on his first kiss, his mother's lullaby. Emotional beat: commodification of the self, made literal.

chapters.title: What I Kept
chapters.summary: Jude inventories what remains: his skill with numbers, his hatred, one afternoon of sunlight. He begins forging entries in the Undercourt's ledger—debts that don't exist. Emotional beat: the taster becomes a counterfeiter.

chapters.title: The King Notices
chapters.summary: The forged debts unravel; the King summons Jude, amused rather than angry, and offers a bargain: serve as the court's permanent ledger-keeper and keep a curated version of himself. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Jude refuses, quoting the guild's founding principle: nothing given freely can be owned. The King's patience ends; the ceiling-stars begin going out one by one, taking memories from everyone above. Emotional beat: defiance with consequences.

chapters.title: Brannic's Bargain
chapters.summary: Brannic secretly offers the King his remaining years in exchange for his daughter's name—and gets it. He returns aged, weeping, triumphant. Emotional beat: love priced honestly at last.

chapters.title: The Daughter's Name
chapters.summary: POV shift to Wren, Brannic's daughter, waking in the capital with her name restored but no idea who gave it. She begins investigating the guild. Emotional beat: a gift arriving without its giver.

chapters.title: Collapse Above
chapters.summary: Wren's POV: the capital deteriorates as stars die—plague returning, wards failing, the Queen dying of a poison no taster caught. Wren finds Jude's abandoned notebooks. Emotional beat: reading a stranger's elegy for himself.

chapters.title: Prison of Mirrors
chapters.summary: The King imprisons Jude in a cell of mirrors showing every version of himself he might have been. Sable visits, confessing she took the same offer he refused and regrets it across four hundred years. Emotional beat: despair answered by witness.

chapters.title: The Founding Entry
chapters.summary: In the mirrors, Jude finds the guild's true founding entry: the first guildmaster sold her own death to start the ledger, meaning every trade since rests on a debt never repaid. Emotional beat: revelation—the whole system is unpaid grief.

chapters.title: Escape by Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Jude proves mathematically that the King's own existence is a debt—the court was purchased from something older and never paid off. The mirrors shatter. Emotional beat: the powerless weaponized.

chapters.title: Revolt of the Sold
chapters.summary: Jude spreads the arithmetic through the Undercourt; the sold souls—generations of them—stop accepting their valuations. The market freezes. Emotional beat: collective refusal as revolution.

chapters.title: Sable Chooses
chapters.summary: Sable turns on the King, giving Jude the master key: her own contract, the oldest one, which chains the court's authority. Emotional beat: redemption bought at the only price left.

chapters.title: Confrontation with the Patient King
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Jude faces the King, who offers finally to simply give him his soul free—an act the system cannot survive. Emotional beat: the trap of accepting kindness from power.

chapters.title: The Unpriced Thing
chapters.summary: Jude refuses even a gift, invoking the founding principle: some things were never for sale, including his mother's choice. He tears the original contract. Emotional beat: the climax's moral core.

chapters.title: Payment in Full
chapters.summary: The court begins collapsing as its currency fails. Jude negotiates one final trade: all the stolen stars returned to the sky in exchange for the court's willing dissolution. Emotional beat: ending a system, not just escaping it.

chapters.title: Ascent
chapters.summary: Jude climbs out carrying Sable's fading form and Brannic's body; Wren meets them at the mouth of the mountain with lanterns. Emotional beat: exhaustion, dawn, the first stars returning overhead.

chapters.title: The Sky Restored
chapters.summary: Stars reignite across the kingdom; memories flood back to those who lost them. Jude remembers the sea, his mother's face, the lullaby—all of it, including the cost. Emotional beat: restoration that includes pain.

chapters.title: Burning the Ledgers
chapters.summary: Jue burns the Hollow Guild's books publicly, freeing every outstanding debt, then surrenders his immunity-ruined body to a healer's slow care. Emotional beat: choosing to be ordinary.

chapters.title: What the Taster Keeps
chapters.summary: Epilogue-adjacent: Jude apprentices Wren in honest accounting—not of souls, but of grain and coin. Sable, mortal now, plants a garden above the sealed mountain. Emotional beat: quiet rebuilding.

chapters.title: A Ember for the Hollow
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Jude's POV. On the anniversary, he tastes the Queen's food one last time as a guest, finds nothing poisoned, and walks home under a full sky, carrying his mother's unredacted name. Emotional beat: peace earned, memory held, survival finally worth its price.
